posts.title: The Agents File Their Own Tickets Now
posts.description: A few months ago I wrote about building an agent in 100 lines of Lisp. It had one tool, lisp-eval, and the fun of it was that the model could write any capability it needed straight into the running program. When I gave it a search key, it wrote its own search function. Asked it to make the CLI better and it would create the most unnecessarily elaborate CLI it could.

posts.title: Thinking Fast and Slow
posts.description: Those of us who spend any time thinking about AI agents tend to think about them as loops around a language model. Something wakes the agent, like a message. The agent sends that message, plus whatever context it has assembled, to a model. The model returns. Maybe it requests a tool, and the tool executes, and the result goes back, and so on. The loop continues until the model decides it is finish
